trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Rome
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

experiences.name: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel
experiences.description: Explore one of the world's greatest art collections, culminating in Michelangelo's breathtaking Sistine Chapel ceiling. Book skip-the-line tickets in advance to maximize your time among Renaissance masterpieces.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 16:00. Rest and travel time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Rome, GA airport at 16:00 on Condor flight. Collect luggage, arrange ground transport, and check in to La Quinta by Wyndham Rome at 15 Chateau Drive. Freshen up and get oriented in the local area around the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Take a relaxed evening stroll around the Chateau Drive neighborhood to get your bearings. Visit a nearby grocery store (Walmart or Kroger) to stock up on snacks, breakfast items, and drinks to save money throughout the trip — a key budget travel hack.

meals.breakfast: Eaten before or during travel — grab something at the airport.
meals.lunch: In-flight meal or airport snack during travel.
meals.dinner: Zaxby's or Chick-fil-A near the hotel on Shorter Ave — quick, affordable, and filling after a long travel day. Budget ~$10–12 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is purely arrival and recovery. Rome, GA is a small city — not Rome, Italy. Note that the hotel address (15 Chateau Drive, Rome, US 34.2212, -85.1513) places you in Rome, Georgia, USA. Plan local activities accordingly. Keep receipts for all expenses to track your budget.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Rome Area History Museum (open 9 AM) on Broad Street downtown — free or low-cost admission. Explore exhibits on the history of Rome, GA and the surrounding Floyd County area. Afterward, walk along the scenic Oostanaula and Etowah River confluence area near downtown.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore downtown Rome's public art scene — the city has numerous murals, sculptures, and the famous Romulus and Remus Wolf Statue (a gift from Benito Mussolini in 1929, a nod to the city's Italian namesake). Walk the Historic District along Broad Street, window-shopping and admiring the architecture. Visit the free Clock Tower atop Neely Hill for panoramic views of the city.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the cool of the evening (expect highs near 30°C, so evenings are more comfortable) with a walk along the Riverwalk trail along the Coosa River. Watch the sunset from the riverbank.

meals.breakfast: Use groceries purchased last night — cereal, fruit, or yogurt in the hotel room. Budget ~$2–3.
meals.lunch: Harvest Moon Café on Broad Street — a local favorite with affordable sandwiches and salads. Budget ~$10–13.
meals.dinner: El Sombrero Mexican Restaurant on Turner McCall Blvd — generous portions at budget-friendly prices. Tacos and enchiladas ~$10–14 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Wear light, breathable clothing — June temperatures average 29.8°C. Carry a reusable water bottle. Downtown Rome is very walkable from the hotel via a short drive or rideshare (~5–10 min).

day_by_day.morning: Head to Myrtle Hill Cemetery (free, open daily) — a stunning hilltop cemetery with sweeping views of Rome and the rivers below. It's a surprisingly beautiful and peaceful art-meets-history experience, with ornate Victorian-era monuments and sculptures. Open early, ideal before the heat peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Chieftains Museum / Major Ridge Home (National Historic Landmark) — a preserved 1794 log cabin and plantation home with exhibits on Cherokee history and culture. Admission is low-cost (~$5–8). Afterward, browse the Rome Farmers Market (Fridays) for local produce, handmade goods, and affordable snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Catch a live music event or art show at a local venue — check the Rome City Auditorium or local Facebook event pages for free or low-cost Friday night events. Rome has an active arts community.

meals.breakfast: Hotel room breakfast with groceries. Budget ~$2–3.
meals.lunch: Grab fresh produce and a snack from the Farmers Market — local bread, fruit, and cheese make a perfect picnic lunch by the river. Budget ~$8–10.
meals.dinner: Schroeder's New Deli on Broad Street — a Rome institution with hearty sandwiches and German-inspired comfort food at reasonable prices. Budget ~$12–15.

day_by_day.notes: The Chieftains Museum connects beautifully to art and history interests. Bring cash for the Farmers Market — many vendors are cash-only. Rain chance exists (~33mm monthly average), so carry a compact umbrella.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Coosa Valley Art Center or explore the Berry College campus (free and open to the public) — one of the largest college campuses in the world by acreage, with stunning Gothic architecture, a working farm, and abundant wildlife including deer. The architecture and grounds are genuinely impressive and completely free to walk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Shorter University Art Gallery or check local listings for any weekend art exhibitions or open studio events in Rome. Rome has a growing arts scene with several galleries. Alternatively, explore the public sculpture trail along the Riverwalk.
day_by_day.evening: Saturday night in downtown Rome — explore the bar and restaurant scene on Broad Street. Many venues have live music on Saturday evenings at no cover charge.

meals.breakfast: Hotel room breakfast. Budget ~$2–3.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch to enjoy on the Berry College campus grounds — use groceries from your stock. Budget ~$3–5.
meals.dinner: Harvest Moon Café or try Broad Street Brewing Company for affordable pub food and local craft beer in a lively Saturday atmosphere. Budget ~$13–16.

day_by_day.notes: Berry College is about 10–15 minutes from the hotel by car. Wear comfortable walking shoes — the campus is vast. Saturday is the best day to find local art events and community gatherings.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed Sunday morning — sleep in, enjoy a hotel room breakfast, then visit the Rome-Floyd County Library which occasionally hosts free art exhibitions and cultural events. Check their calendar in advance. Alternatively, attend a Sunday morning service at one of Rome's historic churches for a free cultural and architectural experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or rideshare to Cave Spring, GA (~20 minutes from Rome) — a charming small town with a natural limestone cave (Rolater Park Cave, very low admission ~$2–3), a natural spring, and a beautiful public park with a swimming pool. The cave is a unique geological art-of-nature experience and a great way to cool off from the heat.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Rome for a quiet Sunday evening. Cook a simple meal using hotel room amenities or groceries, or opt for an affordable takeout option.

meals.breakfast: Hotel room breakfast. Budget ~$2–3.
meals.lunch: Picnic at Rolater Park in Cave Spring — bring sandwiches and snacks from your grocery stock. Budget ~$3–5.
meals.dinner: Takeout from Zaxby's, Moe's Southwest Grill, or another affordable chain near the hotel. Budget ~$10–12. Or cook ramen/pasta in the hotel room to save maximum budget.

day_by_day.notes: Cave Spring is a hidden gem and very budget-friendly. The cave stays cool (~15°C inside) — a welcome relief from summer heat. Bring a light jacket for the cave tour. Sunday hours may vary for some attractions — call ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Coosa Valley Art Center on East 2nd Avenue — Rome's primary dedicated art space with rotating exhibitions, local artist showcases, and sometimes free or low-cost admission. This directly aligns with your art interest and supports the local creative community.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a self-guided food tour of Rome's downtown culinary scene — sample local flavors by visiting 2–3 spots for small bites or drinks. Rome has a surprisingly diverse food scene for a small city. Try a local bakery, a specialty coffee shop, and a local deli or food truck.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset hike or walk at Lock and Dam Park along the Coosa River — a peaceful green space with river views, picnic areas, and walking trails. Free admission. Ideal in the cooler evening hours.

meals.breakfast: Hotel room breakfast. Budget ~$2–3.
meals.lunch: Self-guided food tour — budget ~$15–18 total across multiple small stops. Try Breve Coffee + Kitchen for a light lunch and great coffee.
meals.dinner: Pastime Restaurant on Broad Street — a Rome classic, known for affordable home-style Southern cooking. Meat-and-three style meals ~$10–13.

day_by_day.notes: Monday can be slower for some attractions — call the Coosa Valley Art Center to confirm hours. The food tour approach is a great budget strategy: small portions at multiple places gives variety without overspending. Stay hydrated in the heat.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Rome — revisit your favorite spot from the week for a nostalgic last look. Consider a peaceful walk along the Riverwalk or back up to the Clock Tower for a final panoramic view of the city. Pick up any local souvenirs from downtown shops — look for handmade or locally produced items to support local artists.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of La Quinta (standard checkout 11 AM — confirm with hotel). If your departure allows, spend remaining time exploring any missed spots or doing last-minute souvenir shopping on Broad Street. Store luggage at the hotel lobby if needed while you explore.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Rome, GA. Head to the airport or onward destination. Reflect on a successful budget trip — art, food, history, and nature all explored without breaking the bank.

meals.breakfast: Use up remaining grocery items for a final hotel room breakfast. Budget ~$2–3.
meals.lunch: Final meal in Rome — return to your favorite restaurant from the week, or try one last new spot. Recommended: a final visit to Harvest Moon Café or Pastime Restaurant. Budget ~$12–15.
meals.dinner: Airport or travel meal depending on departure schedule. Budget ~$10–15.

day_by_day.notes: Total estimated daily food budget: ~$25–35/day using the grocery + selective dining strategy. Total 7-day food budget estimate: ~$175–245. Free and low-cost attractions kept activity costs minimal — most days under $15 in admission fees. Rome, GA is a genuinely charming small city with real art, history, and food culture worth exploring on a budget.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 16:00. Rest and travel time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive Rome via Condor flight at 16:00. Transfer to La Quinta by Wyndham Rome, check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll around the immediate hotel neighborhood to get oriented. Pick up any essentials at a nearby pharmacy or convenience store.
day_by_day.evening: Head into central Rome for a relaxed first-night dinner. Explore the area around Piazza Navona on foot — admire the Baroque fountains and street artists as the evening light softens. Keep the evening low-key to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport meal
meals.lunch: N/A — in-flight or airport meal
meals.dinner: Osteria del Pegno near Piazza Navona — a mid-range Roman trattoria serving classic cacio e pepe and saltimbocca. Budget ~€25–35 per person including house wine.

day_by_day.notes: Given the 16:00 arrival, allow at least 90 minutes for baggage claim, ground transport, and hotel check-in before planning any activity. Rome in late June averages 29.8°C highs, so pack light breathable clothing. Keep Day 1 relaxed to avoid jet lag fatigue.

day_by_day.morning: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel (pre-booked skip-the-line entry, opens 09:00). Spend 3–4 hours exploring one of the world's greatest art collections — the Gallery of Maps, Raphael Rooms, and culminating in Michelangelo's breathtaking Sistine Chapel ceiling. Arrive early to beat the midday crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Vatican, cross the Tiber and walk through the charming Prati neighborhood. Visit Castel Sant'Angelo (exterior and bridge) for scenic photos. Rest in the shade along the riverbank during the hottest part of the day (typically 13:00–15:30). Then explore St. Peter's Square and Basilica (free entry) if energy allows.
day_by_day.evening: Wander into the Prati district for aperitivo hour (18:30–19:30) — a Campari spritz and free snacks at a local bar. Dinner in Prati, a neighborhood beloved by locals.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby Roman bar — cornetto and cappuccino (~€3–5)
meals.lunch: Il Sorpasso in Prati — a beloved local spot with excellent sandwiches, salumi boards, and natural wines. Budget ~€15–20 per person.
meals.dinner: Ristorante Il Matriciano in Prati — a classic Roman restaurant famous for its amatriciana and gricia pasta. Budget ~€30–40 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Vatican Museums tickets should be booked online in advance (official website: museivaticani.va). Dress code required for Sistine Chapel and St. Peter's Basilica — cover shoulders and knees. Bring a refillable water bottle; Rome has free drinking fountains (nasoni) throughout the city.

day_by_day.morning: Borghese Gallery Art Experience (pre-booked timed entry — mandatory, max 2 hours per session, opens 09:00). Visit this intimate world-class gallery housing Bernini's dramatic sculptures (Apollo and Daphne, The Rape of Proserpina) and Caravaggio paintings inside a stunning villa. One of Rome's most rewarding art experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the gallery, stroll through the beautiful Villa Borghese gardens — Rome's green lung. Rent a rowboat on the lake (~€5) or simply relax under the umbrella pines. Walk or take a short taxi to the Spanish Steps and the Trevi Fountain area. Toss a coin at Trevi (best visited mid-afternoon when slightly less crowded than evening).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the elegant Via Condotti shopping street (window shopping is free!) and the atmospheric streets around the Pantheon. Visit the Pantheon itself (check current entry fee/hours). Dinner in the historic center.

meals.breakfast: Antico Caffè Greco near the Spanish Steps — one of Rome's oldest cafés, perfect for a pre-gallery espresso and pastry (~€5–8)
meals.lunch: Picnic in Villa Borghese gardens — pick up supplies from a nearby deli or Mercato Trionfale: fresh bread, prosciutto, pecorino, fruit (~€10–12 per person)
meals.dinner: Armando al Pantheon — a beloved family-run Roman institution near the Pantheon serving traditional carciofi alla romana and rigatoni con pajata. Reserve ahead. Budget ~€35–45 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery tickets MUST be booked in advance at galleriaborghese.it — they sell out days or weeks ahead. Entry is strictly timed (2-hour slots). The gallery is a 10-minute walk from the Villa Borghese gardens entrance. Wear comfortable shoes — today involves significant walking.

day_by_day.morning: Campo de' Fiori Market & Cooking Class. Start at 09:00 at the vibrant Campo de' Fiori market, selecting fresh seasonal ingredients — zucchini blossoms, pecorino, local tomatoes, fresh pasta. Then join a hands-on cooking class (typically 3–4 hours) learning to prepare a full Roman meal: antipasto, fresh pasta, and a classic secondo.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the cooking class (which typically includes eating your creations as lunch!), take a leisurely afternoon to digest and explore the Jewish Ghetto neighborhood nearby — one of Rome's most historically layered districts. Visit the Portico d'Ottavia ruins and browse the area's unique shops and bakeries.
day_by_day.evening: Cross the Tiber to Trastevere for the evening. This bohemian neighborhood comes alive at night with locals and visitors alike. Explore the medieval streets, visit the stunning Santa Maria in Trastevere basilica (free, beautifully lit at night), and enjoy a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before the market — grab a cornetto and espresso at a bar near Campo de' Fiori (~€3–4)
meals.lunch: Included as part of the cooking class experience (you eat what you cook — a full Roman meal with wine)
meals.dinner: Da Enzo al 29 in Trastevere — a legendary neighborhood trattoria with excellent cacio e pepe and coda alla vaccinara. Reserve well in advance. Budget ~€28–38 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Campo de' Fiori market runs Monday–Saturday mornings until about 13:00. The cooking class should be pre-booked through providers like Cookly or Airbnb Experiences (~€80–120 per person). Saturday evening in Trastevere is lively — arrive at your restaurant reservation on time as tables turn quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Trastevere Food Walking Tour. Join a guided food walking tour through Trastevere's cobblestone streets (typically starts 10:00–10:30, lasts 3 hours). Sample supplì (Roman fried rice balls), carciofi alla giudia (Jewish-style fried artichokes), fresh ricotta, local cheeses, and finish with a classic gelato. Learn the neighborhood's history through its food culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the tour, visit the nearby Gianicolo Hill (Janiculum) for the best panoramic views over Rome's rooftops — a hidden gem that most tourists miss. The walk up is about 20 minutes or take a taxi. Enjoy the breeze and views, then head back down for a quiet afternoon rest during peak heat (13:00–16:00). Visit the Palazzo Corsini or simply browse antique shops along Via della Lungara.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the historic center for a final evening stroll. Visit Piazza Navona at dusk when the light is golden and street performers are out. Enjoy a leisurely Sunday dinner in the centro storico.

meals.breakfast: Light — coffee and pastry before the food tour begins (the tour itself includes substantial tastings)
meals.lunch: Covered by the Trastevere Food Walking Tour tastings — you'll be well-fed by tour's end around 13:00–13:30
meals.dinner: Osteria dell'Enoteca Corsi near the Pantheon — a no-frills, cash-only Roman lunch spot that also opens Sunday evenings; daily specials on a chalkboard, excellent value. Budget ~€20–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Sunday in Rome means many churches are open for free (including Santa Maria in Trastevere with its stunning 12th-century mosaics). Some shops and smaller restaurants may be closed Sunday afternoon. The Trastevere Food Tour should be pre-booked (~€75–95 per person). Gianicolo cannon fires at noon daily — a Roman tradition worth witnessing.

day_by_day.morning: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Guided Art Walk. Join a small-group guided tour (typically 09:00–12:30) of the Roman Forum and Palatine Hill, uncovering ancient frescoes, mosaics, and architectural masterpieces. A knowledgeable guide brings the ruins to life — far more rewarding than exploring alone. The Colosseum exterior is visible from Palatine Hill.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the tour, visit the Colosseum (add-on ticket if not included in your Forum pass — book in advance). Explore the Celio neighborhood nearby — quieter and more residential, with the beautiful Basilica di Santi Giovanni e Paolo. Rest during the hottest hours (14:00–16:00) at a café or in the shade of the Circus Maximus park.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Testaccio neighborhood — Rome's authentic working-class food district. Browse the Testaccio Market (closes by 14:00 but the neighborhood is lively all evening). This is Rome's best neighborhood for traditional offal-based Roman cuisine and excellent wine bars.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a quick bar stop near the hotel — fuel up before the morning tour
meals.lunch: Flavio al Velavevodetto in Testaccio — a beloved trattoria built into Monte Testaccio (a hill made of ancient amphora shards), serving exceptional Roman classics. Budget ~€25–35 per person.
meals.dinner: Roscioli Salumeria con Cucina in the centro storico — a legendary deli-restaurant hybrid with extraordinary cured meats, cheeses, and pasta. Reserve well ahead. Budget ~€40–50 per person including wine.

day_by_day.notes: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum tickets must be booked in advance at coopculture.it — the same ticket covers the Forum, Palatine Hill, and Colosseum. Monday can be busy as some museums are closed (Borghese is open). Wear sturdy shoes — the Forum terrain is uneven cobblestone. Bring sun protection; the Forum has very little shade.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Rome — revisit a favorite neighborhood or spot at a relaxed pace. Consider the quieter Aventine Hill for the famous Knights of Malta keyhole view of St. Peter's dome, and the beautiful Orange Garden (Giardino degli Aranci) with sweeping city views. Alternatively, browse the antique book stalls along Lungotevere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping in the centro storico — artisan food shops near Campo de' Fiori for olive oils, pasta, and local wines to bring home. Visit any remaining must-see spots. Begin packing and preparing for departure. Check out of hotel and arrange transport to airport if departing today.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a restaurant that encapsulates your Roman experience — a neighborhood spot you've grown to love during the week, or a new discovery. Raise a glass of local Frascati white wine to the trip.

meals.breakfast: Forno Campo de' Fiori — Rome's most famous bakery, open early, serving extraordinary pizza bianca and maritozzi (cream-filled buns). A perfect final Roman breakfast (~€5–8)
meals.lunch: Supplì Roma near the Pantheon — the city's best supplì (fried risotto balls) and pizza al taglio for a casual, affordable final lunch (~€10–15 per person)
meals.dinner: Trattoria Moderna in Trastevere or return to a favorite from the week — budget ~€30–40 per person. Toast with a digestivo (limoncello or amaro) to close the Roman chapter.

day_by_day.notes: If your return flight is on June 22, confirm departure time and allow at least 2.5–3 hours before flight for Rome airport (FCO/Fiumicino) transport and check-in. The Leonardo Express train from Termini to FCO takes 32 minutes and runs every 15 minutes (~€14). Keep final day flexible and unhurried — Rome rewards those who slow down.

Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll around the immediate neighborhood to orient yourself and shake off any travel fatigue.
day_by_day.evening: Ease into Rome with a relaxed first dinner at a nearby upscale restaurant. Enjoy a glass of Frascati DOC white wine on a terrace as the golden-hour light fades. After dinner, take a short evening walk to admire illuminated local landmarks and piazzas before an early night to rest for the days ahead.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight or airport meal
meals.lunch: Not applicable — in-flight or airport meal
meals.dinner: Dinner at a premium local trattoria near the hotel — order Roman classics such as cacio e pepe, saltimbocca alla romana, and a tiramisu to finish. Pair with a bottle of Cesanese del Piglio red wine.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Confirm your pre-booked private airport transfer in advance. Tip: request a late check-in guarantee with the hotel so your room is ready upon arrival regardless of any flight delays. Pack a light linen layer for the evening as temperatures can drop slightly after sunset.

day_by_day.morning: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel — Begin with an exclusive early-access skip-the-line guided tour of the Vatican Museums. Spend 2–3 hours moving through the Gallery of Maps, Raphael Rooms, and culminating in a breathtaking private-feeling moment inside the Sistine Chapel beneath Michelangelo's ceiling. A knowledgeable art historian guide will provide rich context throughout.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Vatican, cross the Tiber via the Ponte Sant'Angelo and explore the Castel Sant'Angelo at your own pace. Then head into the Prati neighborhood — Rome's upscale district near the Vatican — for a leisurely afternoon gelato stop at a premium artisan gelateria before returning to the hotel to rest during the hottest part of the day (around 29–30°C).
day_by_day.evening: Dress for a sophisticated dinner in the Prati or Trastevere area. Enjoy a multi-course tasting menu at a Michelin-recognized restaurant, featuring seasonal Roman cuisine with modern flair — think house-made pasta, local sea bass, and a curated wine pairing.

meals.breakfast: Full Italian breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café — cornetto, cappuccino, fresh-squeezed orange juice, and seasonal fruit.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a premium wine bar (enoteca) near the Vatican — bruschetta, burrata, charcuterie board, and a glass of Vermentino.
meals.dinner: Tasting menu dinner at a Michelin-starred or highly acclaimed restaurant in Prati — 5–7 courses with wine pairing. Budget approximately €120–€180 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book Vatican Museums early-access tickets well in advance — they sell out weeks ahead, especially in June. Dress code for the Sistine Chapel: covered shoulders and knees required. Carry a small bottle of water and a folding fan given the summer heat.

day_by_day.morning: Campo de' Fiori Market & Cooking Class — Start the morning at the vibrant Campo de' Fiori market, one of Rome's most atmospheric open-air markets. With a private chef guide, hand-select fresh seasonal produce, local cheeses, cured meats, and fragrant herbs. Then transfer to a premium cooking school kitchen for a hands-on class preparing a full Roman menu: antipasto, fresh pasta (tonnarelli or rigatoni), a main course, and dessert.
day_by_day.afternoon: After your cooking class lunch, walk off the meal with a leisurely stroll through the historic center. Visit the nearby Piazza Navona to admire Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers, then explore the Pantheon (book timed entry in advance). Duck into the cool interior for a moment of awe before the afternoon heat peaks.
day_by_day.evening: Aperitivo hour at a rooftop bar with panoramic views over Rome's skyline — sip a Negroni or Aperol Spritz as the sun sets over the terracotta rooftops. Follow with dinner at a celebrated restaurant specializing in Roman Jewish cuisine near the historic Ghetto neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel, then a tasting session of market produce at Campo de' Fiori — sample supplì, seasonal fruit, and local cheeses.
meals.lunch: The dishes you prepare during the cooking class served as a full sit-down lunch with wine — included in the experience.
meals.dinner: Roman Jewish cuisine dinner in the Ghetto neighborhood — carciofi alla giudia (deep-fried artichokes), baccalà in tomato sauce, and ricotta e visciole tart. Pair with a crisp Greco di Tufo white wine.

day_by_day.notes: The cooking class typically runs 10:00–14:00. Wear comfortable shoes for the market visit on cobblestones. The Pantheon requires a timed entry ticket (book online). June evenings are warm and perfect for rooftop aperitivo — reserve a rooftop bar table in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Borghese Gallery Art Experience — Visit the world-class Borghese Gallery, set within the lush Villa Borghese gardens. This intimate gallery strictly limits visitor numbers, making it one of Rome's most exclusive art experiences. Marvel at Bernini's breathtaking sculptures (Apollo and Daphne, The Rape of Proserpina) and Caravaggio's dramatic masterpieces. A private guide will illuminate the stories and techniques behind each work over a 2-hour curated tour.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the gallery, rent a rowboat on the Villa Borghese lake or take a leisurely electric golf cart tour through the park — a perfect way to enjoy the greenery while avoiding the midday heat. Then head to the elegant Via Veneto or Parioli neighborhood for a premium afternoon coffee and pastry at a historic café.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Spanish Steps at dusk when the crowds thin and the atmosphere becomes magical. Browse the luxury boutiques along Via Condotti (Valentino, Bulgari, Gucci) for an evening shopping stroll. Dinner at a refined restaurant near the Trevi Fountain — toss a coin for good luck before your meal.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel — full spread including eggs, pastries, cold cuts, cheeses, and fresh juice.
meals.lunch: Elegant lunch at a restaurant within or adjacent to Villa Borghese park — seasonal salads, grilled fish, and chilled rosé wine.
meals.dinner: Upscale dinner near the Trevi Fountain or Spanish Steps — fresh seafood antipasto, house-made fettuccine with black truffle, and a classic panna cotta. Wine pairing with a Barolo or Brunello di Montalcino.

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery tickets MUST be booked weeks in advance — entry is strictly timed and limited to 360 visitors per 2-hour slot. Arrive 15 minutes early. The gallery is closed on Mondays. Villa Borghese park is a wonderful escape from the city heat — bring sunscreen and a hat.

day_by_day.morning: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Guided Art Walk — Join a small-group (or private) expert-guided tour of the Roman Forum and Palatine Hill. Your art historian guide will bring ancient Rome to life, uncovering surviving frescoes in imperial palaces, intricate mosaic floors, and the architectural grandeur of the Forum. Palatine Hill offers sweeping panoramic views over the Colosseum and the city — arrive early (08:30) to beat the heat and crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the ancient sites, visit the nearby Circus Maximus and take a short taxi to the Aventine Hill — a quiet, aristocratic neighborhood. Stroll through the Orange Garden (Giardino degli Aranci) for one of Rome's best panoramic views, and peek through the famous Knights of Malta keyhole for a perfectly framed view of St. Peter's dome. Return to the hotel for a mid-afternoon rest and pool time if available.
day_by_day.evening: Trastevere Food Walking Tour — As the evening cools, join a premium small-group food tour through the enchanting cobblestone streets of Trastevere. Sample supplì (Roman fried rice balls), carciofi alla romana, aged pecorino, local wines, and artisan gelato at carefully curated stops. Your guide will share the neighborhood's history and culinary secrets.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before the 08:30 tour start — keep it light with yogurt, fruit, and a double espresso.
meals.lunch: Post-tour lunch at a premium trattoria in the Testaccio neighborhood — Rome's traditional food district. Try pajata (if adventurous), coda alla vaccinara (oxtail stew), and supplì. Pair with a carafe of house Frascati.
meals.dinner: The Trastevere Food Walking Tour includes multiple tastings that serve as a progressive dinner — conclude with a final glass of local wine at a candlelit enoteca in Trastevere.

day_by_day.notes: The Roman Forum/Palatine Hill/Colosseum ticket is combined — book online in advance to skip queues. Wear sturdy walking shoes as the ancient sites have uneven terrain. Sunday mornings are relatively quieter at the Forum. The Trastevere tour typically runs 18:00–21:00, perfectly timed for the cooler evening hours.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate the morning to a curated private art gallery experience in Rome's contemporary and classical art scene. Visit the Palazzo Doria Pamphilj — a private palace still owned by the noble Doria Pamphilj family, housing an extraordinary collection including Velázquez's portrait of Pope Innocent X and works by Caravaggio, Titian, and Raphael. The audio guide is narrated by a family member, making it uniquely personal.
day_by_day.afternoon: Indulge in a premium Roman spa and wellness experience — book a 2-hour treatment at one of Rome's luxury hotel spas (such as those at the St. Regis or Hassler Roma) for a massage, thermal bath, or beauty treatment. This is the perfect mid-trip recharge. Alternatively, explore the Capitoline Museums on Capitoline Hill — the world's oldest public museums, housing the iconic bronze Marcus Aurelius statue and stunning views over the Forum.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-eve splurge: reserve a table at one of Rome's most celebrated fine dining restaurants for a landmark meal. Opt for a chef's tasting menu with full wine pairing — this is the pinnacle dining experience of the trip. Dress elegantly and savor every course.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast — take your time this morning with a full spread and a second cappuccino.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium enoteca near the Palazzo Doria Pamphilj — charcuterie, aged cheeses, truffle crostini, and a glass of aged Chianti Classico Riserva.
meals.dinner: Flagship fine dining experience — 8–10 course chef's tasting menu at a Michelin-starred restaurant (e.g., La Pergola, Il Pagliaccio, or Acquolina). Budget €200–€300+ per person with wine pairing. Reserve months in advance.

day_by_day.notes: La Pergola (Rome's only 3-Michelin-star restaurant) requires reservations made months ahead — if not already booked, check for cancellations or opt for Il Pagliaccio (2 stars) or Acquolina (1 star, seafood-focused). Palazzo Doria Pamphilj is closed on Thursdays. Dress code for fine dining: smart elegant attire required.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Rome — wake up early for one last espresso ritual at a classic Roman bar, standing at the counter like a local. Take a slow, nostalgic walk through your favorite neighborhood or revisit a piazza that captured your heart. Visit any last-minute sites or shops — pick up premium souvenirs such as artisan leather goods, local wines, aged balsamic, or handmade ceramics from quality boutiques.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure time, enjoy a final leisurely lunch at a beloved restaurant. Check out of the hotel and arrange your private luxury transfer back to Fiumicino Airport. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for Rome traffic and airport procedures.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Rome — carry the flavors, art, and memories of an extraordinary week in the Eternal City.

meals.breakfast: Final Roman breakfast standing at a historic café bar — cornetto integrale (whole wheat croissant) with crema, and a perfectly pulled ristretto.
meals.lunch: Last lunch at a beloved trattoria — order your favorite dish from the week, perhaps a final plate of cacio e pepe or carbonara, with a glass of chilled Vermentino. Finish with a scoop of pistachio gelato for the road.
meals.dinner: In-flight or at the airport — consider purchasing premium Italian provisions (local salumi, cheese, wine) from a gourmet airport shop for the journey home.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your return flight details and arrange the airport transfer the evening before. Rome traffic can be unpredictable — allow extra time. Duty-free at Fiumicino has excellent Italian wine and food selections. Keep liquids within airline regulations if purchasing olive oil or wine. Arrivederci, Roma!
